html:
The Makuna, who call themselves Yeba-masã, are a Tucanoan-speaking people of the Pirá Paraná and Apaporis rivers in the Vaupés region of Colombia and nearby Brazil.

They live in longhouses, or malocas, and farm manioc, fish and hunt. Like other peoples of the region, they marry outside their own language group, so many people speak several languages. Their shamans keep a detailed knowledge of the forest and rivers as sacred places. In 2011 UNESCO listed the traditional knowledge of the jaguar shamans of Yuruparí of the Pirá Paraná. Neighbours include the Desana and the Cabiyarí.
sum: The Makuna, who call themselves Yeba-masã, are a Tucanoan-speaking people of the Pirá Paraná and Apaporis rivers in the Vaupés region of Colombia and nearby Brazil.
